key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Rapid onset over hours. LOCATION: Supraglottic region. DURATION: Acute, hours to days. CHARACTER: Severe throat pain, dysphagia, dyspnea. AGGRAVATING: Swallowing, lying flat. RELIEVING: Sitting upright, humidified air, antibiotics. TIMING: Acute, progressive. SEVERITY: Severe (8-10/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: High fever, drooling, stridor, dysphagia, muffled voice, tripod positioning, anxiety. KEY POSITIVES: High fever, drooling, stridor, dysphagia, tripod positioning. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain, no wheezing.
